response: Yes, CT can predict the level of CSF block in tuberculous hydrocephalus. CT scans can help identify the location and extent of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) blockage, which is often caused by tubercular meningitis or other inflammatory processes. By visualizing the ventricular system and any areas of obstruction, CT scans can aid in determining the level of CSF blockage, guiding further management and potential surgical intervention.
